column11: derived: JNJ generated $56,725mm of free cash flow on $263,004mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 21.57% margin, against the 23.4% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: JNJ paid $5,540mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.07% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.11% to 0.04%. Restated at replacement capex: JNJ spent $13,799mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $8,728mm of depreciation and amortisation less amortisation of intangibles, 1.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 0.04% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: JNJ's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $6,000mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,500mm; 2024 instalment 2,000mm; 2025 instalment 2,500mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 27.17% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 31.91%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.74%. It was held at nil, but JNJ books $4,600mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000200406-26-000016), 4.88% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.74%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 JNJ's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,811mm, inventories up $3,901mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $6,344mm, a working capital build of $368mm, 0.14% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -4.74% to -4.88%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.2766 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3207 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -4.4065%.

The Balversa label (DailyMed set id 2a8aa5c0-6c92-4566-8c45-e8f4d1fc20ee, spl version 14, effective 2025-11-17, the row the book's labels table carries) indicates it 'for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) with susceptible FGFR3 genetic alterations whose disease has progressed on or after at least one line of prior systemic therapy'. Both gate studies are the opposite end of the disease and exclude that population outright. MoonRISe-3 (NCT06919965) excludes the 'presence or history of histologically confirmed, muscle-invasive, locally advanced, nonresectable, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (that is [i.e.], T2, T3, T4, N+, and/or M+)', and MoonRISe-1 (NCT06319820) enrols intermediate-risk Ta low-grade disease with all visible papillary tumour resected. A tumour has invaded beyond the lamina propria or it has not, so in any one year the two pools are disjoint

Four published inputs, then one chain for each study. (1) 84,530 estimated new US bladder cancers for the year, SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Bladder Cancer, the incidence data/epidemiology.csv carries for Urinary Bladder Neoplasms. (2) The non-muscle-invasive share, 75%: Nielsen ME, Smith AB, Meyer AM, Kuo TM, Tyree S, Kim WY, Milowsky MI, Pruthi RS, Millikan RC, 'Trends in stage-specific incidence rates for urothelial carcinoma of the bladder in the United States: 1988 to 2006', Cancer 2014;120(1):86-95 (doi 10.1002/cncr.28397, PMID 24122346), 'approximately 75% of incident cases found to be superficial to the muscularis propria at the time of presentation'; the same citation jnj_inlexzo.csv uses for the complement. 84,530 x 0.75 = 63,398 a year. (3) The risk-group split: van Hoogstraten LMC, Vermeulen SH, Hof JP, van der Heijden AG, Vrieling A, Kiemeney LA, Aben KKH, 'Surveillance patterns in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer across risk groups: a real-world analysis', BJU Int 2026;138(2):257-266 (doi 10.1111/bju.70297, PMID 42024120, PMC13371837), Table 2 on 2,791 Dutch NMIBC tumours: 'All NMIBCs (N = 2791) LR (N = 431) IR (N = 1035) HR/very HR (N = 1325)', so intermediate risk 37.083% and high or very high risk 47.474%. (4) FGFR3 alteration by grade and stage, which both studies require: Pietzak EJ, Bagrodia A, Cha EK et al., 'Next-generation Sequencing of Nonmuscle Invasive Bladder Cancer Reveals Potential Biomarkers and Rational Therapeutic Targets', Eur Urol 2017;72(6):952-959 (doi 10.1016/j.eururo.2017.05.032, PMID 28583311, PMC6007852), 105 prospectively sequenced MSKCC NMIBC tumours: 'FGFR3 mutations were associated with lower grade and stage (LGTa = 83% [19/23]; HGTa = 59% [19/32]; HGT1 = 34% [13/38]...)' and 'alterations in FGFR3 were seen in 39% (32/82) of high-grade NMIBC'. MoonRISe-1 (NCT06319820, intermediate-risk Ta low grade): 63,398 x 0.37083 x 19/23 = 19,421 a year. MoonRISe-3 (NCT06919965, papillary-only high-risk, prior BCG): 63,398 x 0.47474 x 32/82 x 0.60 = 7,047 a year, where 0.60 is US BCG receipt in high-grade NMIBC in 2017, from Kennedy-Yoon D, Almohtasib J, Kaul S et al., 'Association of Patient, Disease, and Socioeconomic Characteristics With Receipt of Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin Therapy From 2002-2017 and the Impact of BCG Supply Shortages', Urology 2026;213:88-95 (doi 10.1016/j.urology.2026.04.010, PMID 41990884), 16,958 SEER-Medicare adults 66 and over with newly diagnosed high-grade NMIBC: 'BCG receipt increased from 37% in 2002 to 60% in 2017 in eligible patients'. The two populations are disjoint by risk group, so they add: 26,468 a year, over 25,000, is 1.05874
column12: READ THIS BEFORE USING THE NUMBER. It is the row this layer turns on and it has four soft joints. (a) The risk-group split is Dutch and tumour-level, counting recurrences as well as primaries; no US split of incident NMIBC by AUA or EAU risk group is published in a free source, and I looked. (b) The FGFR3 shares are one US academic centre, 105 tumours, and the LGTa cell is 19 of 23. Johnson and Johnson's own press release of 2026-03-13 puts FGFR alterations at 'approximately 70 percent of intermediate-risk and 40 percent of high-risk' NMIBC, which is higher than Pietzak on the intermediate side; its primary citation is an EAU congress abstract (Roupret M et al., Eur Urol 2022;87(S1):A0673) that could not be opened, so the peer-reviewed figures are taken and the row errs LOW against the sponsor's own. (c) Three of each study's filters are NOT cut, for want of published shares, and all three run the same way: MoonRISe-3's requirement that patients be 'ineligible for or refusing radical cystectomy', MoonRISe-3's exclusion of any CIS, and MoonRISe-1's requirement of a named recurrence or size risk factor for the Ta LG/G2 arm. So the row errs HIGH on those. On the CIS exclusion specifically the overcount is small, because the FGFR filter already removes nearly all of it: Billerey C, Chopin D, Aubriot-Lorton MH et al., Am J Pathol 2001;158(6):1955-1959 (doi 10.1016/S0002-9440(10)64665-2, PMID 11395371, PMC1891972) found FGFR3 mutations in '0 of 20, 0%' of CIS against '37 of 50, 74%' of pTa. (d) The 60% BCG figure is SEER-Medicare, so 66 and over, and it is the 2017 endpoint of a rising series. One row, two catalysts: 967 (MoonRISe-3, 2028-04-06) and 995 (MoonRISe-1, 2028-06-28) share this asset-indication pair and both are covered here

column11: ANCHOR, measured, in the larger of the two gate populations. Bree KK, Shan Y, Hensley PJ et al., 'Management, Surveillance Patterns, and Costs Associated With Low-Grade Papillary Stage Ta Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Among Older Adults, 2004-2013', JAMA Netw Open 2022;5(3):e223050 (doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.3050, PMID 35302627, PMC8933744), 13,054 SEER-Medicare patients aged 66 to 90 diagnosed with low-grade Ta NMIBC: 'With regard to treatment, 2250 patients (17.2%) received intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guerin, and 792 patients (6.1%) received intravesical chemotherapy (excluding receipt of a single perioperative dose).' 17.2% is the measured US reach of the incumbent intravesical agent in exactly the population MoonRISe-1 enrols, which is 73% of this layer's eligible patients. It is taken as the share a new intravesical system reaches at peak. Two independent checks in the same disease land within a point and a half of it and are checks rather than sources: Inlexzo's own 18.658% reach in its approved non-muscle-invasive segment, and the 17.8% jnj_inlexzo.csv carries for the muscle-invasive bladder-sparing population
column12: a judgement, and here is which way each half errs. It errs LOW on the MoonRISe-3 limb, 27% of the eligible pool, where the incumbent reaches far more of the population: BCG receipt in high-grade NMIBC was 60% by 2017 on the Kennedy-Yoon series, so a drug competing there has a much larger treated segment to take from. It errs HIGH on the MoonRISe-1 limb, because 17.2% is BCG uptake and TAR-210's comparator there is intravesical chemotherapy, which the same paper measures at only 6.1%; most intermediate-risk patients today get surveillance and repeat resection rather than any agent, so a new system must create demand rather than displace it. The two directions do not cancel and I have not netted them. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT PRICE: the product sold into this indication is TAR-210, an erdafitinib intravesical delivery system, not the oral tablet Balversa's label and this asset's price and stopping rate are measured on. jnj_balversa.csv's own base_pool_overlap_pct note already flags that. A reviewer should settle the price against the system before using the value this penetration produces
